name: Kedarkantha
season: December to April for snow; April-June is also possible
summary: A popular winter trek in the Govind Pashu Vihar area with pine forest, a frozen lake and a summit with wide views. Often chosen as a first snow trek.
highlights: Pine and oak forests in snow
Summit panorama of Swargarohini and Bandarpoonch
start: Sankri village; Dehradun to Sankri is a long mountain drive of roughly 190 km, usually 9-10 hours.

stages.title: Drive Dehradun to Sankri
stages.text: Long road day via Purola. Arrive in the evening and stay in a homestay.

stages.title: Sankri to Juda ka Talab
stages.text: A few hours of walking through forest to a frozen lake campsite.

stages.title: Juda ka Talab to Kedarkantha Base
stages.text: Short walk to the base camp; acclimatise and rest.

stages.title: Summit and descend to Hargaon
stages.text: Early start for the summit, then a long descent. This is the longest day.

stages.title: Hargaon to Sankri and drive back
stages.text: Walk down to Sankri and drive back or stay another night.

stay: Camping on the trek; homestays at Sankri.
facilities: Basic toilet tents on organised treks; no electricity or reliable network after Sankri.
permits: Entry is controlled by the forest department; operators normally arrange fees. Confirm current permit rules.
safety: Do not trek independently in snow; use a registered operator and guide.
Carry layers and waterproof gloves.
cost: Operator-run treks usually charge a package fee that includes transport from the base, food and guides. Get written quotes and inclusions.
responsible: Do not leave the trail or camp outside designated spots.

faq.a: Yes with a registered operator and good fitness. The summit day is long.

name: Har Ki Dun
season: April to June and September to November; winter is for experienced groups
summary: A valley trek through the Supin river valley with traditional villages, forest and views at the head of a glacial valley. It is a longer and quieter trek than Kedarkantha.
highlights: Ancient wooden villages such as Osla
Meadows and peaks at the valley head
start: Sankri village; same long drive as Kedarkantha.

stages.title: Drive to Sankri
stages.text: Long drive from Dehradun via Purola.

stages.title: Sankri to Taluka and walk to Seema
stages.text: Short drive and a walk along the river.

stages.title: Seema to Har Ki Dun via Osla
stages.text: A longer day with a gradual climb.

stages.title: Explore and rest
stages.text: Walk up to the glacier head and return to camp.

stages.title: Return via Osla and Seema
stages.text: Descent along the same route.

stages.title: Drive back
stages.text: Return to Dehradun.

stay: Camping and village homestays on organised treks.
facilities: Limited. Carry what you need; no reliable phone network.
permits: Forest entry fees apply; operators normally handle them.
safety: River crossings can be dangerous in monsoon and snow.
Do not trek alone.
cost: Package prices vary by operator; compare inclusions and group size.
responsible: Respect village customs, do not disturb sacred sites.
suits: Fit beginners looking for a longer trek

faq.q: Is Har Ki Dun harder than Kedarkantha?
faq.a: It is longer and has more days at altitude. Fitness requirements are higher.

name: Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Trek
distance: about 13 km to Ghangaria, plus day walks
altitudeNote: Valley about 3,600 m; Hemkund about 4,300 m
season: June to October; bloom is usually July to September
summary: A trek to a protected alpine valley known for its flowers, with an optional climb to Hemkund Sahib. The route is busy in season because many pilgrims walk it too.
start: Govindghat, about an hour from Joshimath by road.

stages.title: Reach Joshimath
stages.text: Long drive from Rishikesh.

stages.title: Govindghat to Ghangaria
stages.text: About 13 km walk or pony ride on a steady path.

stages.title: Valley of Flowers
stages.text: Walk into the valley and return to Ghangaria the same day.

stages.title: Hemkund Sahib
stages.text: Steep climb from Ghangaria and return.

stages.title: Ghangaria to Govindghat
stages.text: Walk down and drive to Joshimath.

stay: Lodges and the gurdwara at Ghangaria.
facilities: Shops, lodges and a small medical facility at Ghangaria in season; limited network.
permits: Entry needs a permit, bought online or at the forest counter in Ghangaria. The park opened 1 June 2026 and was reported open to 31 October; entry is reported 7 am to 2 pm with exit by about 5 pm, and overnight stays in the valley are not allowed. Fees are reported inconsistently (confirm with the forest department).
safety: Landslides can block the Govindghat trail.
Do not stay in the valley after dark.
cost: Costs depend on lodging and pony hire; check current rates locally.

faq.a: Usually July to August, but it varies year to year.

name: Kuari Pass
season: March to June and September to December; snow in winter
summary: A ridge trek along the 'Curzon trail' with long views of Nanda Devi, Dronagiri and other peaks. It starts from the Joshimath side and suits moderately fit trekkers.
highlights: Panoramas of the Nanda Devi group

stages.title: Joshimath to Gulling top
stages.text: A steady climb to the first camp.

stages.title: Gulling to Khullara
stages.text: Ridge walk through forest.

stages.title: Khullara to Kuari Pass
stages.text: Climb to the pass and views.

stages.title: Pass to Tali
stages.text: Descent through forest and meadows.

stages.title: Tali to Auli
stages.text: Walk out near Auli and drive back.

facilities: No facilities on the route; carry everything.
permits: Check forest department requirements; operators usually arrange them.
safety: Snow and ice are common in winter.
Check Joshimath advisories before starting.
responsible: Do not light fires in the forest.

faq.q: Is Kuari Pass good in winter?
faq.a: Yes for snow, but trails can be icy and you need a guide.

name: Nag Tibba
season: October to March; summer is hot
summary: A short weekend trek close to Dehradun and Mussoorie. A good first trek for beginners and families with fit children.
highlights: Views of the Bandarpoonch range on clear days
start: Pantwari village, roughly 85-90 km from Dehradun (about 3-4 hours).

stages.title: Pantwari to Nag Tibba base
stages.text: A steady climb through forest to the campsite.

stages.title: Summit and return
stages.text: Early walk to the summit and descent to Pantwari.

facilities: Basic; no network on the upper trail.
permits: Check local forest rules; operators usually handle them.
safety: Do not trek in poor weather.
Carry water.
cost: Short guided trips are cheaper than the multi-day treks; confirm inclusions.
suits: Weekend trips from Dehradun or Delhi

faq.q: Can I do Nag Tibba in a day?
faq.a: It can be done in a long day but a night at the campsite is more relaxed.

name: Dayara Bugyal
season: Most of the year; deep snow in winter, green meadows in summer
summary: A high meadow trek above Uttarkashi with broad open slopes and views of the Bandarpoonch and Gangotri ranges. Good for beginners who want a meadow trek.
highlights: Snow in winter, flowers in summer
start: Barsu village near Raithal, about 30-35 km from Uttarkashi.

stages.title: Uttarkashi to Barsu
stages.text: Drive to Barsu and rest.

stages.title: Barsu to Gui Pass
stages.text: A climb to the first campsite.

stages.title: Gui to Dayara and back
stages.text: Walk onto the meadow and return to camp.

stages.title: Return to Barsu
stages.text: Descent and drive back.

safety: Whiteout is possible in snow; do not leave the route.
Lightning is a risk on open meadows in monsoon.
cost: Operator packages are widely available; compare inclusions.
responsible: Stay on established paths; the meadow is fragile.

faq.q: Can I see snow at Dayara?
faq.a: Yes in winter and early spring; check conditions.

name: Brahmatal
season: December to March for snow; April-June for green
summary: A winter trek in the Kumaon-Garhwal border area with frozen lakes, Mount Trishul views and an oak forest. Popular for snow in winter.
highlights: Frozen lakes at Bekaltal and Brahmatal
Views of Mount Trishul and Nanda Ghunti
start: Lohajung village, a long drive from Kathgodam or Haridwar.

stages.title: Reach Lohajung
stages.text: Long drive via Gwaldam.

stages.title: Lohajung to Bekaltal
stages.text: Climb to the lake campsite.

stages.title: Bekaltal to Brahmatal
stages.text: Longer walk across the ridge.

stages.title: Summit day
stages.text: Climb to the ridge for views and return.

stages.title: Descent to Lohajung
stages.text: Walk out.

stages.title: Drive back
stages.text: Return.

permits: Check forest department requirements; operators handle them.
safety: Winter nights are very cold.
Do not trek without a guide in snow.

faq.a: With a guide and good fitness, yes. Nights are cold.

name: Chopta-Tungnath-Chandrashila
distance: about 10 km round trip from Chopta to Chandrashila
altitudeNote: Tungnath about 3,680 m; Chandrashila about 4,000 m
season: Most of the year; temple closed in winter; snow December to March
summary: A short trek to the Tungnath temple and on to the Chandrashila summit. It is one of the easiest ways to reach 4,000 m in Uttarakhand.
start: Chopta, with Tungnath about 3.5-4 km on foot.

stages.title: Drive to Chopta
stages.text: Long road day via Ukhimath.

stages.title: Chopta to Tungnath and Chandrashila
stages.text: Steady climb on a paved trail; return to Chopta.

stages.title: Explore or leave
stages.text: Short walks or begin the return.

stay: Small hotels, camps and GMVN lodge.
facilities: Basic eateries at Tungnath and Chopta; limited network.
permits: No special trek permit is typically needed; confirm locally.
safety: Snow hides the trail in winter.
Start early to avoid afternoon clouds.
cost: No operator is strictly needed; guides are optional in summer.
responsible: Do not litter; plastic waste is a problem here.

faq.a: The trail is open but snow-covered; the temple is closed.

name: Pindari Glacier
season: April to June and September to October
summary: A long valley trek in Kumaon to the Pindari glacier snout, with river valleys, villages and forest.
highlights: Views of Nanda Kot and Panwali Dwar
start: Bageshwar, then a road to Song or Loharkhet.

stages.title: Bageshwar to Loharkhet/Dhakuri
stages.text: Drive and short walk.

stages.title: Dhakuri to Khati
stages.text: Walk along the valley.

stages.title: Khati to Dwali
stages.text: Gradual climb along the river.

stages.title: Dwali to Phurkia
stages.text: Higher camp on the trail.

stages.title: Phurkia to Zero Point and back
stages.text: A long walk to the glacier.

stages.title: Return
stages.text: Descent via the same route.

stay: KMVN huts and camps along the route.
permits: Check forest and local permit requirements.
safety: Landslides and rivers in monsoon.
Altitude gain is gradual but real.
cost: Costs vary with operator and lodging.
responsible: Take litter out; avoid camp fires.

faq.a: Less than the Garhwal treks, though May-June sees more groups.

name: Milam Glacier
season: May to June and September to October
summary: A remote trek up the Johar valley to Milam village and the Milam glacier. Long days, a border area, and a permit are involved. Best for experienced trekkers with an operator.
highlights: Remote Johar valley and Bhotiya villages
Views of Hardeol and Trishuli peaks
start: Munsiyari, then road and trail via Lilam.

stages.title: Reach Munsiyari
stages.text: Long drive from Kathgodam or Pithoragarh.

stages.title: Munsiyari to Lilam and Bogdiar
stages.text: Start of the valley route.

stages.title: Bogdiar to Martoli and Milam
stages.text: Long walking days with villages.

stages.title: Glacier day
stages.text: Walk to the glacier and return.

stages.title: Return
stages.text: Descent via the same route.

facilities: Very limited; no network on most of the route.
permits: Reports conflict on the Inner Line Permit: one report says the ITBP stopped requiring it for tourists going up to Milam, while operators still list it. Confirm with the Munsiyari SDM office and carry ID and photos.
safety: Remote area with very limited rescue options.
Do not attempt unsupported.
cost: Packages from specialist operators; confirm inclusions.
responsible: Respect local residents and the border-area rules.

faq.q: Can I do Milam without a permit?
faq.a: Reports conflict. Check with the Munsiyari SDM office before you go.

name: Auden's Col
season: May-June and September-October for experienced teams
summary: An advanced, high-altitude crossing between the Gangotri and Bhilangna valleys. It involves glacier travel and technical sections. Not for independent trekkers.

stages.title: Multi-day expedition
stages.text: This is an expedition-level route. Plan only with a recognised mountaineering operator, experienced guides and required permits.

permits: The Gangotri National Park permit rules apply (reported daily cap of 150 for Gaumukh-Tapovan); expedition-level routes need special permission. Confirm with the Uttarkashi forest office and a mountaineering operator.
safety: Glacier crevasses, rockfall, altitude and weather make this dangerous.
Do not attempt without mountaineering experience and an expedition operator.

faq.q: Can I do Auden's Col on my own?
faq.a: No. It requires mountaineering skills and an expedition operator.
